claim: Chronologically aging yeast cells undergo a sudden redox collapse that affects over 80% of identified thiol-containing proteins.
source_text: Here, we report the discovery that chronologically aging yeast cells undergo a sudden redox collapse, which affects over 80% of identified thiol-containing proteins.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental OxICAT measurements conducted on yeast cells during chronological aging, as detailed in the manuscript's results section.

claim: The redox collapse is not triggered by an increase in endogenous oxidants as postulated by the free radical theory of aging.
source_text: We present evidence that this redox collapse is not triggered by an increase in endogenous oxidants as would have been postulated by the free radical theory of aging.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on experimental data showing NADPH depletion rather than ROS increase, combined with inference that contradicts the free radical theory.

claim: The redox collapse is instigated by a substantial drop in cellular NADPH.
source_text: Instead it appears to be instigated by a substantial drop in cellular NADPH, which normally provides the electron source for maintaining cellular redox homeostasis.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by direct measurements of NADPH levels during chronological aging showing a decrease that precedes protein oxidation.

claim: The decrease in NADPH levels occurs very early during lifespan and sets into motion a cascade that down-regulates most cellular processes.
source_text: This decrease in NADPH levels occurs very early during lifespan and sets into motion a cascade that is predicted to down-regulate most cellular processes.
evidence_reasoning: Based on temporal measurements of NADPH levels and subsequent protein oxidation patterns, with inference about downstream effects.

claim: Caloric restriction increases NADPH levels and delays each facet of the cascade.
source_text: Caloric restriction, a near-universal lifespan extending measure, increases NADPH levels and delays each facet of the cascade.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental measurements comparing NADPH levels and protein oxidation timing under standard vs. caloric restriction conditions.

claim: The system-wide oxidation of the proteome occurs days before cell death.
source_text: Our studies reveal a time line of events leading up to the system-wide oxidation of the proteome days before cell death.
evidence_reasoning: Based on temporal OxICAT measurements correlated with viability assays showing oxidation precedes death.

claim: The free radical theory of aging postulates that aging is caused by an accumulation of oxidative damage to cellular macromolecules.
source_text: One leading hypothesis is the free radical theory of aging, which postulates that aging is caused by an accumulation of oxidative damage to cellular macromolecules (Harman, 1956).
evidence_reasoning: This is a well-established theory in the field, supported by citation to Harman, 1956.

claim: Recent studies in mice have generated conflicting results regarding the effects of genetic manipulations targeting conserved antioxidant genes on lifespan.
source_text: However, while these studies confirm the general notion that oxidative damage is associated with aging, recent studies in mice have generated conflicting results as few of the genetic manipulations targeting conserved antioxidant genes showed the predicted effects on lifespan (Perez et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to Perez et al., 2009, describing experimental results in mice.

claim: Chronological lifespan is defined as the length of time that non-dividing cells remain viable in a high metabolic state.
source_text: Chronological lifespan is defined as the length of time that non-dividing cells remain viable in a high metabolic state (Fabrizio and Longo, 2007; Fontana et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is a standard definition in the field, supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Chronological lifespan decreases in yeast strains lacking the oxidant scavenging enzymes superoxide dismutase (SOD) or catalase.
source_text: In support of the free radical theory of aging, chronological lifespan decreases in yeast strains lacking the oxidant scavenging enzymes superoxide dismutase (SOD) or catalase (Longo et al., 1996)
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to Longo et al., 1996, describing experimental results in yeast mutants.

claim: Chronological lifespan increases when glutathione or SOD levels are elevated.
source_text: chronological lifespan decreases in yeast strains lacking the oxidant scavenging enzymes superoxide dismutase (SOD) or catalase (Longo et al., 1996) and increases when glutathione or SOD levels are elevated (Harris et al., 2003).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to Harris et al., 2003, describing experimental manipulations of antioxidant levels.

claim: Caloric restriction significantly increases chronological lifespan in yeast.
source_text: Also, caloric restriction, a nearly universal measure to extend lifespan, has been shown to significantly increase chronological lifespan in yeast (Fontana et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to Fontana et al., 2010, describing caloric restriction effects in yeast.

claim: Calorically restricted organisms show significantly increased oxidative stress resistance.
source_text: Although the molecular mechanism by which caloric restriction extends lifespan has not been elucidated, one unifying trait among calorically restricted organisms is a significantly increased oxidative stress resistance (Barja, 2002).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to Barja, 2002, describing a common trait across calorically restricted organisms.

claim: Yeast cells undergo a global redox collapse that leads to massive thiol oxidation in almost 80% of identified proteins several days prior to cell death.
source_text: By monitoring the thiol oxidation status of almost 300 different protein thiols, we discovered that yeast cells undergo a global redox collapse that leads to massive thiol oxidation in almost 80% of identified proteins several days prior to cell death.
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT measurements of protein thiol oxidation status during chronological aging.

claim: The general protein oxidation is preceded by the oxidation of a subset of conserved proteins, including NADPH-dependent thioredoxin reductase.
source_text: Cluster analysis revealed that this general protein oxidation is preceded by the oxidation of a subset of conserved proteins, one of which is NADPH-dependent thioredoxin reductase, a key enzyme in maintaining redox homeostasis.
evidence_reasoning: Based on cluster analysis of temporal OxICAT data showing distinct oxidation patterns.

claim: Protein oxidation is triggered by a decrease in cellular NADPH concentration.
source_text: Redox metabolite and NADPH studies suggested that protein oxidation is triggered by a decrease in cellular NADPH concentration.
evidence_reasoning: Based on measurements of NADPH levels and their temporal correlation with protein oxidation events.

claim: Caloric restriction delayed NADPH decrease, early protein oxidation, global redox collapse, and cell death.
source_text: Consistent with this hypothesis, caloric restriction delayed NADPH decrease, early protein oxidation, global redox collapse, and cell death.
evidence_reasoning: Based on comparative measurements between standard and caloric restriction conditions.

claim: The decrease in cellular NADPH levels initiates oxidation of the cellular redox machinery and triggers system-wide oxidation events.
source_text: Our results suggest that the decrease in cellular NADPH levels initiates oxidation of the cellular redox machinery and triggers system-wide oxidation events, which significantly precede cell death.
evidence_reasoning: Based on temporal correlation of NADPH depletion with redox machinery oxidation and subsequent proteome-wide oxidation.

claim: OxICAT is based on the differential modification of in vivo reduced and in vivo oxidized cysteine thiols with isotopically light 12C and isotopically heavy 13C versions of ICAT.
source_text: OxICAT is based on the differential modification of in vivo reduced and in vivo oxidized cysteine thiols, respectively with isotopically light 12C and isotopically heavy 13C versions of the isotope-coded affinity tag (ICAT) thiol alkylating reagent
evidence_reasoning: This describes the established methodology of the OxICAT technique.

claim: The ratio of in vivo reduced to oxidized protein thiols is unaffected by changes in relative protein amounts.
source_text: Because this ratio is unaffected by changes in relative protein amounts, OxICAT is uniquely suited to simultaneously monitor changes in the thiol oxidation status of hundreds of proteins over time.
evidence_reasoning: This is a property of the ratiometric measurement approach inherent to the OxICAT method.

claim: Almost 400 thiol-containing peptides in about 290 different yeast proteins were previously identified and quantified for steady-state oxidation level.
source_text: We had previously identified and quantified the steady-state oxidation level of almost 400 thiol-containing peptides in about 290 different yeast proteins localized to various cellular and subcellular compartments (Brandes et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: Refers to prior work by the same authors, supported by citation and previous experimental data.

claim: DB746 cells maintain their high metabolic, postdiauxic state until they die with a mean lifespan of approximately 7 days under standard conditions.
source_text: Under standard conditions, 2% glucose SCD media is used and DB746 cells maintain their high metabolic, postdiauxic state until they die (mean lifespan ∼7 days)
evidence_reasoning: Based on experimental measurements of cell viability over time under standard cultivation conditions.

claim: GapDH contains two redox-sensitive cysteines (the active site Cys150 and the nearby Cys154).
source_text: GapDH contains two redox-sensitive cysteines (the active site Cys150 and the nearby Cys154), and both of these are found in the same tryptic peptide (GapDH144–160).
evidence_reasoning: Based on established knowledge of GapDH structure and confirmed by the authors' previous experimental work.

claim: The two redox-sensitive cysteines in GapDH form an intramolecular disulfide bond during peroxide stress in vivo.
source_text: We previously suggested that these cysteines form an intramolecular disulfide bond during peroxide stress in vivo (Brandes et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: Based on previous experimental work by the authors, supported by citation.

claim: During the first 2 days of cultivation under either standard or caloric restriction conditions, less than 30% of the two GapDH cysteines were oxidized.
source_text: During the first 2 days of cultivation under either standard or caloric restriction conditions, we found that the GapDH144–160 peptide was predominantly labeled with two light ICAT molecule and less than 30% of the two cysteines were calculated to be oxidized
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT measurements of GapDH oxidation status during early chronological aging.

claim: Within 24 hours on day 3 of cultivation under standard conditions, about 70% of the GapDH peptide became oxidized.
source_text: However, within the next 24 hr (i.e., day 3) of cultivation under standard conditions, about 70% of the GapDH peptide was labeled with two heavy ICAT molecules, indicating that both cysteines were oxidized
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT measurements showing rapid increase in GapDH oxidation.

claim: On day 4 under standard conditions, over 80% of all GapDH molecules were oxidized.
source_text: On day 4 under standard conditions, over 80% of all GapDH molecules were oxidized, indicating that by that time, glycolysis is dramatically reduced.
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT measurements with inference about the functional consequence for glycolysis.

claim: The oxidation status of GapDH from yeast cells cultivated under caloric restriction conditions remained low for the first 4 days of cultivation.
source_text: In contrast, the oxidation status of GapDH from yeast cells cultivated under caloric restriction conditions remained low for the first 4 days of cultivation
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT measurements under caloric restriction conditions.

claim: Under caloric restriction, significant GapDH oxidation occurred within a 24-hour time window, with over 70% affected by day 5 and almost 90% by day 7.
source_text: Then, however, significant oxidation occurred (also within a 24-hr time window), with over 70% of all GapDH molecules affected by day 5 and almost 90% affected by day 7
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT measurements showing delayed but rapid oxidation under caloric restriction.

claim: Yeast cells cultivated in water showed no significant increase in GapDH oxidation over the monitored time span.
source_text: Yeast cells cultivated in standard media for 2 days and then switched into water showed no significant increase in GapDH oxidation over the time span that was monitored by OxICAT
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT measurements of cells shifted to hypometabolic water conditions.

claim: Under hypometabolic conditions, cells maintain GapDH in its reduced and active state over extended periods of time.
source_text: suggesting that under hypometabolic conditions, cells maintain GapDH in its reduced and active state over extended periods of time.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from OxICAT data showing maintained reduced state of GapDH in water.

claim: 286 protein thiols were reproducibly identified in all samples taken under standard 2% glucose conditions.
source_text: We reproducibly identified 286 of these protein thiols in all samples taken under standard 2% glucose conditions (i.e., all four replicates at five different time points)
evidence_reasoning: Based on mass spectrometry identification across multiple replicates and time points.

claim: Over 40 oxidation-sensitive proteins play crucial roles in protein translation.
source_text: For instance, we found over 40 oxidation-sensitive proteins that play crucial roles in protein translation, including 27 different thiol-containing 40S, 60S, and 54S ribosomal proteins, several translation initiation (e.g., TIF11, GCD1) and elongation factors (e.g., EFT2, TEF1, TEF3), translational activators (e.g., GCN1), and numerous tRNA synthetases (e.g., MES1, KRS1, VAS1).
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT identification and functional annotation of oxidized proteins.

claim: Oxidation of translation-related proteins likely affects the rate and extent of protein synthesis in chronologically aging yeast cells.
source_text: Oxidation of these proteins most likely affects the rate and extent of protein synthesis in chronologically aging yeast cells.
evidence_reasoning: Logical inference based on the known functions of the oxidized proteins.

claim: Numerous metabolic enzymes become oxidized, likely affecting processes ranging from the Krebs cycle and the pentose phosphate pathway to fatty acid and amino acid synthesis.
source_text: Moreover, we found countless metabolic enzymes, including ACO1, PGK1, IDP1, PDC1, and TPI1 to become oxidized, likely affecting processes ranging from the Krebs cycle and the pentose phosphate pathway to fatty acid and amino acid synthesis.
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT data identifying oxidized metabolic enzymes with inference about functional consequences.

claim: Over 33% of the 290 monitored protein thiols have been confirmed to be redox-sensitive in yeast or other organisms.
source_text: In fact, of the 290 different protein thiols that we monitored in our study, over 33% have been confirmed to be redox-sensitive in yeast or other organisms
evidence_reasoning: Based on comparison of the authors' data with the RedoxDB database.

claim: An additional 20% of identified cysteines are localized to proteins that contain redox-sensitive cysteines whose specific positions have not yet been fully identified.
source_text: Moreover, an additional 20% of our identified cysteines are localized to proteins that have been found to contain redox-sensitive cysteines but whose redox-sensitive cysteines have not yet been fully identified.
evidence_reasoning: Based on comparison with RedoxDB database showing partial characterization of redox-sensitive proteins.

claim: Over 80% of an unbiased population of thiol-containing yeast proteins have the capacity to become significantly oxidized under physiologically relevant growth conditions.
source_text: Our finding that over 80% of an unbiased population of thiol-containing yeast proteins have the capacity to become significantly oxidized under physiologically relevant growth conditions (Figure 1—Source data 1) suggests that reversible cysteine oxidation, such as that detected with our OxICAT method, is a much more widespread event than previously anticipated.
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT data with inference about the prevalence of reversible cysteine oxidation.

claim: Chronologically aging yeast cells are metabolically active in the stationary phase.
source_text: Despite the limited supply of nutrients in the stationary phase, oxygen consumption measurements indicate that chronologically aging yeast cells are metabolically active in this phase (Fabrizio et al., 2003; Fabrizio and Longo, 2003).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citations to studies measuring oxygen consumption in aging yeast.

claim: Intracellular ATP is maintained at levels equivalent to or above those present during exponential growth for up to 5 days under standard conditions and for at least 7 days under caloric restriction conditions.
source_text: Consistent with earlier ATP measurements conducted in chronologically aging yeast cells (Goldberg et al., 2009), we found that intracellular ATP is indeed maintained at levels equivalent to or above those present during exponential growth for up to 5 days when cultivated under standard postmitotic growth conditions and for at least 7 days under caloric restriction conditions
evidence_reasoning: Based on ATP measurements in this study, consistent with previous literature.

claim: Chronologically aging yeast cells are able to maintain their energy resources and survive for extended periods despite a heavily oxidized proteome.
source_text: These results demonstrate that chronologically aging yeast cells are not starving and are able to maintain their energy resources and survive for extended periods of times despite (or possibly even because of) a heavily oxidized proteome.
evidence_reasoning: Based on ATP and viability measurements combined with OxICAT data showing oxidized proteome.

claim: The majority of protein thiols in yeast show low oxidation for the initial 2 days then suddenly increase by day 3 in standard media or by day 5 in caloric restriction media.
source_text: Analysis of the kinetics of protein thiol oxidation revealed that the majority of protein thiols in yeast follow the trend observed for GapDH oxidation: the thiol oxidation state is low for the initial 2 days of cultivation then suddenly increases by day 3 in standard media or by day 5 in caloric restriction media.
evidence_reasoning: Based on temporal OxICAT analysis of multiple protein thiols.

claim: Several protein thiols undergo oxidation that precedes the global wave of oxidation by 24-48 hours.
source_text: In addition, however, we noticed several protein thiols whose oxidation appeared to precede this global wave of oxidation by 24–48 hr
evidence_reasoning: Based on cluster analysis of temporal OxICAT data showing distinct early oxidation patterns.

claim: Over 70% of peptides fall into clusters A-C showing oxidation patterns consistent with the global redox collapse.
source_text: Over 70% of peptides fall into clusters A–C.
evidence_reasoning: Based on k-means clustering analysis of OxICAT data.

claim: Analysis of subcellular distribution of proteins in individual clusters did not reveal significant correlation between protein location and oxidation pattern.
source_text: Analysis of the subcellular distribution of the proteins in the individual clusters did not reveal any significant correlation between the location of the proteins and their oxidation pattern (apart from the expected accumulation of proteins of the endoplasmic reticulum and secreted proteins in cluster G)
evidence_reasoning: Based on analysis of subcellular localization data for proteins in different oxidation clusters.

claim: Proteins in cluster G (ER and secreted proteins) are expected to accumulate in an oxidized state.
source_text: apart from the expected accumulation of proteins of the endoplasmic reticulum and secreted proteins in cluster G
evidence_reasoning: Based on established knowledge that the ER is an oxidizing environment for protein folding.

claim: Cysteines in clusters D and E are significantly more conserved than cysteines in clusters A and B.
source_text: In-depth analysis of the cysteine's pKa values, solvent accessibility, and the amino acid sequence surrounding the identified cysteines revealed that cysteines in clusters D and E are significantly more conserved than cysteines in clusters A and B
evidence_reasoning: Based on bioinformatic analysis of sequence conservation around identified cysteines.

claim: Cysteines in clusters D and E are more frequently flanked by positively charged amino acids than cysteines in clusters A and B.
source_text: Moreover, cysteines in clusters D and E are more frequently flanked by positively charged amino acids than cysteines in clusters A and B
evidence_reasoning: Based on amino acid composition analysis of sequences flanking identified cysteines.

claim: Positively charged amino acids in the vicinity of cysteines are known to lower the pKa of the thiol group and increase its reactivity.
source_text: Positively charged amino acids in the vicinity of cysteines are known to lower the pKa of the thiol group and increase its reactivity
evidence_reasoning: Based on established biochemical principles of thiol reactivity.

claim: The increased conservation and reactivity of cysteines in clusters D and E suggest they might play important functional roles.
source_text: The increased conservation and reactivity of cysteines in clusters D and E suggest they might play important functional roles
evidence_reasoning: Logical inference from the observed conservation and chemical properties of these cysteines.

claim: Oxidation of at least 28 proteins significantly preceded the general oxidation of proteins under standard or caloric restriction conditions.
source_text: Oxidation of at least 28 proteins significantly preceded the general oxidation of proteins under standard or caloric restriction conditions
evidence_reasoning: Based on cluster analysis identifying proteins in clusters D and E with early oxidation.

claim: Thioredoxin reductase is one of the earliest proteins to become oxidized during chronological aging.
source_text: One of the earliest proteins to become oxidized during chronological aging is thioredoxin reductase
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT measurements showing early oxidation of thioredoxin reductase.

claim: Thioredoxin reductase is a key enzyme in maintaining cellular redox homeostasis.
source_text: thioredoxin reductase, a key enzyme in maintaining cellular redox homeostasis
evidence_reasoning: Based on established knowledge of thioredoxin reductase function in redox biology.

claim: The active site cysteines of thioredoxin reductase (Cys142/Cys145) showed increased oxidation by day 2 under standard conditions.
source_text: The active site cysteines of thioredoxin reductase (Cys142/Cys145) showed increased oxidation by day 2 under standard conditions
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT measurements of thioredoxin reductase active site oxidation.

claim: Shifting cultures from standard media to water on day 2 largely reversed the increased thiol oxidation of thioredoxin reductase within 24 hours.
source_text: Within 24 hr after shifting cultures to hypometabolic cultivation conditions (day 3), the increased thiol oxidation of thioredoxin reductase's active site cysteines observed at day 2 is largely reversed.
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT measurements comparing oxidation before and after shift to water.

claim: Early protein oxidation is, at least in its initial stage, a fully reversible event in yeast.
source_text: It was intriguing to observe that early protein oxidation is, at least in its initial stage, a fully reversible event in yeast.
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT data showing reversal of oxidation upon shift to hypometabolic conditions.

claim: Deletion of cytosolic thioredoxin reductase (TRR1) caused severe growth defects and a significantly shortened lifespan.
source_text: We found that while Δtrr2 mutants grew like wild-type yeast cells and had a wild-type like chronological lifespan, deletion of the cytosolic TRR1 homologue (Δtrr1) caused severe growth defects and a significantly shortened lifespan
evidence_reasoning: Based on experimental measurements of growth and lifespan in deletion mutants.

claim: Δtrr2 mutants grew like wild-type yeast cells and had a wild-type like chronological lifespan.
source_text: We found that while Δtrr2 mutants grew like wild-type yeast cells and had a wild-type like chronological lifespan
evidence_reasoning: Based on experimental measurements of growth and lifespan in deletion mutants.

claim: Healthy-looking Δtrr1 suppressors were generated with very high frequency.
source_text: Moreover, we observed the generation of healthy-looking Δtrr1 suppressors with very high frequency.
evidence_reasoning: Based on observations during cultivation of Δtrr1 deletion mutants.

claim: Cultivation of Δtrr1 deletion mutants without suppressor generation was only possible when the medium was supplemented with cysteine.
source_text: In fact, cultivation of Δtrr1 deletion mutants without the potential generation of suppressors was only possible when the medium was supplemented with cysteine, presumably to maintain proteins in their reduced state.
evidence_reasoning: Based on experimental observations with inference about the role of cysteine supplementation.

claim: Organisms lacking thioredoxin reductase are either severely compromised in growth or non-viable.
source_text: Organisms lacking thioredoxin reductase have previously been shown to be either severely compromised in growth or non-viable (Holmgren and Lu, 2010).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to Holmgren and Lu, 2010, describing effects of thioredoxin reductase deletion.

claim: The NADPH-dependent thioredoxin system is one of two highly conserved multi-enzyme systems that contribute to cellular redox homeostasis in most organisms.
source_text: The NADPH-dependent thioredoxin system is one of two highly conserved multi-enzyme systems that contribute to the maintenance of cellular redox homeostasis in most pro- and eukaryotic organisms.
evidence_reasoning: Based on established knowledge of cellular redox systems.

claim: The other redox system consists of NADPH-dependent glutathione reductase, several small glutaredoxins, and glutathione.
source_text: The other system consists of NADPH-dependent glutathione reductase, several small glutaredoxins, and the cysteine-containing tripeptide glutathione (GSH), which together with its oxidized counterpart GSSG determines the cellular redox potential
evidence_reasoning: Based on established knowledge of the glutathione redox system.

claim: Glutathione together with its oxidized counterpart GSSG determines the cellular redox potential.
source_text: the cysteine-containing tripeptide glutathione (GSH), which together with its oxidized counterpart GSSG determines the cellular redox potential
evidence_reasoning: Based on established biochemical principles of cellular redox potential.

claim: The cellular redox potential (EGSH) remained relatively constant during the first 2 days of cultivation under standard conditions.
source_text: We found that the cellular redox potential (EGSH) remained relatively constant during the first 2 days of cultivation under standard conditions
evidence_reasoning: Based on measurements of GSH and GSSG levels and calculation of redox potential.

claim: The cellular redox potential became significantly more oxidizing by day 3 under standard conditions.
source_text: then became significantly more oxidizing by day 3
evidence_reasoning: Based on measurements of GSH and GSSG levels and calculation of redox potential.

claim: Under caloric restriction conditions, the cellular redox potential remained relatively constant for the first 4 days then became more oxidizing by day 5.
source_text: Under caloric restriction conditions, the cellular redox potential remained relatively constant for the first 4 days then became more oxidizing by day 5
evidence_reasoning: Based on measurements of GSH and GSSG levels under caloric restriction conditions.

claim: Both thioredoxin reductase and glutathione reductase draw their reducing power from NADPH.
source_text: Both thioredoxin reductase and glutathione reductase draw their reducing power from NADPH, making the oxidation status of these systems ultimately dependent on cellular NADPH and NADP+ levels.
evidence_reasoning: Based on established knowledge of NADPH-dependent reductase enzymes.

claim: The oxidation status of thioredoxin and glutathione systems is ultimately dependent on cellular NADPH and NADP+ levels.
source_text: making the oxidation status of these systems ultimately dependent on cellular NADPH and NADP+ levels.
evidence_reasoning: Logical inference from the NADPH-dependence of the reductase enzymes.

claim: Exponentially growing yeast cells have very similar levels of NADPH and NADP+ independent of their initial glucose availability.
source_text: We found that exponentially growing yeast cells have very similar levels of NADPH and NADP+ independent of their initial glucose availability
evidence_reasoning: Based on measurements of NADPH and NADP+ levels in exponentially growing cells.

claim: NADPH and NADP+ levels increased over the 12 hours following exponential growth under both cultivation conditions.
source_text: and that these levels increased over the next 12 hr under both cultivation conditions
evidence_reasoning: Based on temporal measurements of NADPH and NADP+ levels.

claim: Yeast cells undergo a diauxic shift from glucose-driven fermentation to ethanol-driven respiration during the 12 hours following exponential growth.
source_text: In this time frame, yeast cells undergo a diauxic shift from glucose-driven fermentation to ethanol-driven respiration.
evidence_reasoning: Based on established knowledge of yeast metabolism and the diauxic shift.

claim: Cells induce NADH kinases, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase, and cytosolic NADPH-dependent isocitrate dehydrogenase to increase NADPH production during the diauxic shift.
source_text: Cells induce NADH kinases such as UTR1 and POS5, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (ZWF1), and the cytosolic NADPH-dependent isocitrate dehydrogenase (Idp2) to increase NADPH production and regeneration (Gasch et al., 2000).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to Gasch et al., 2000, describing gene expression changes during diauxic shift.

claim: In cells cultivated under standard conditions, intracellular NADPH levels rapidly decreased over the 24-hour period following the diauxic shift.
source_text: In cells cultivated under standard conditions, the intracellular levels of NADPH then rapidly decreased over the next 24-hr time period.
evidence_reasoning: Based on temporal measurements of NADPH levels under standard conditions.

claim: In cells cultivated under caloric restriction conditions, NADPH levels decreased with much slower rates and reached concentrations comparable to standard media with about a 48-hour delay.
source_text: In contrast, in cells cultivated under caloric restriction conditions, NADPH levels decreased with much slower rates and reached concentrations comparable to those observed in standard media with about a 48-hr delay
evidence_reasoning: Based on temporal measurements of NADPH levels under caloric restriction conditions.

claim: The drop in intracellular NADPH levels coincided with the initial oxidation of thioredoxin reductase and the alteration in cellular redox potential.
source_text: This drop in intracellular NADPH levels coincided well with the initial oxidation of thioredoxin reductase and the alteration in the cellular redox potential.
evidence_reasoning: Based on temporal correlation of NADPH measurements with thioredoxin reductase oxidation and redox potential changes.

claim: Early changes in cellular NADPH levels might serve as trigger for the initial oxidation of thioredoxin reductase and changes in cellular redox potential.
source_text: In summary, these results suggest that early changes in cellular NADPH levels might serve as trigger for the initial oxidation of thioredoxin reductase and changes in the cellular redox potential, which subsequently leads to the redox collapse observed in postmitotic yeast cells.
evidence_reasoning: Inference based on temporal correlation of NADPH depletion with subsequent redox events.

claim: Cultivation under caloric restriction conditions delays the decrease in cellular NADPH levels, delays the redox collapse, and extends lifespan.
source_text: Cultivation under caloric restriction conditions appears to delay the decrease in cellular NADPH levels, delays the redox collapse of the yeast proteome, and extends lifespan.
evidence_reasoning: Based on comparative measurements of NADPH, protein oxidation, and lifespan under different conditions.

claim: More than 80% of viable cells were recovered from day 3- and day 4-old cultures despite an almost fully oxidized thiol proteome.
source_text: Moreover, we found that more than 80% of viable cells were recovered from day 3- and day 4-old cultures despite an almost fully oxidized thiol proteome.
evidence_reasoning: Based on viability measurements correlated with OxICAT data showing high oxidation.

claim: The initially reversible thiol modifications might represent a 'pro-active' response to protect proteins against irreversible modifications and extend lifespan.
source_text: It is thus tempting to speculate that the initially reversible thiol modifications that we observe in chronologically aging yeast cells might in fact represent a 'pro-active' response of yeast cells to protect their proteins against irreversible protein modifications and damage, and thereby extend lifespan.
evidence_reasoning: This is explicitly presented as speculation based on the observed reversibility of oxidation.

claim: Over 50% of protein thiols undergo reversible thiol modifications in diamide-treated HeLa and HEK cells.
source_text: Quantitative studies conducted in diamide-treated HeLa and HEK cells revealed that over 50% of protein thiols undergo reversible thiol modifications in response to diamide stress
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to Hansen et al., 2009, describing redox proteomic studies in mammalian cells.

claim: The combined redox proteome of mammalian cells has a higher redox buffering capacity than glutathione.
source_text: providing evidence that the combined redox proteome of mammalian cells has a higher redox buffering capacity than glutathione (Hansen et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to Hansen et al., 2009, describing redox buffering capacity.

claim: The majority of yeast protein thiols have the capacity to undergo reversible redox modifications and serve as redox buffer.
source_text: our data suggest that the majority of yeast protein thiols have the capacity to undergo reversible redox modifications and thereby serve as redox buffer.
evidence_reasoning: Inference based on OxICAT data showing widespread reversible oxidation of protein thiols.

claim: Chronological aging might represent a physiological stress condition that utilizes and stresses the redox buffering capacity of the thiol proteome.
source_text: These results suggest that chronological aging might represent a physiological stress condition that utilizes and stresses the redox buffering capacity of the thiol proteome.
evidence_reasoning: Speculative inference based on the observed widespread protein oxidation during aging.

claim: Oxidation of methionyl-tRNA synthetase (MES1) Cys353 reaches over 65% at day 2 of cultivation in standard conditions.
source_text: One such example would be methionyl-tRNA synthetase (MES1), an enzyme involved in translational initiation (Delarue, 1995) whose oxidation of Cys353 reaches over 65% at day 2 of cultivation in standard conditions
evidence_reasoning: Based on OxICAT measurements of MES1 oxidation.

claim: Cys353 in MES1 is part of a zinc finger-like CX2C-X9-CX2C motif.
source_text: Intriguingly, Cys353 is part of a zinc finger-like CX2C-X9-CX2C motif
evidence_reasoning: Based on sequence analysis and structural knowledge of MES1.

source_text: whose substitution in the E. coli homologue MetRS causes a strong decrease in enzyme activity (Fourmy et al., 1993).

claim: Down-regulation of protein translation contributes to increased oxidative stress resistance and extends lifespan in replicative aging yeast and other organisms.
source_text: Down-regulation of protein translation has been shown to contribute to increased oxidative stress resistance and to extend lifespan in replicative aging yeast and other organisms (Steffen et al., 2008).
evidence_reasoning: Supported by citation to Steffen et al., 2008, describing effects of translation down-regulation.
